title: Printing a value is the same as returning it
statement: A function gives its result back by printing it, so a function that prints its answer can be used in an expression, and return is just another way to display.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: use the result of a function that prints instead of returning
evidence_patterns.signature: expects the printed value to be available to the caller

example.item:
def double(n):
    print(n * 2)
x = double(4)
print(x + 1)

evidence_patterns.item_shape: write a function that should return a value
evidence_patterns.signature: prints the value and omits return

example.item: Write square(n) so that square(3) + 1 is 10.

discriminators.vs_slip: A slip is one missing return the learner spots on rereading. The belief is a stated equivalence ('print gives it back') and persists after seeing None.

conflicts_with.label: return hands a value back to the caller and ends the call

resolved_by.label: return hands a value back to the caller and ends the call
